sentences.text: Since these appeals are arising out of a common accident and common judgment and award, they are clubbed together and disposed of by a common judgment.

2. MFA.No.200106/2021 is filed by legal representative of deceased, while MFA No.200004/2021 and MFA No.200005/2021 are filed by injured seeking enhancement of the compensation granted in respect of the motor vehicle accident dated 12.11.2017.
3. For the sake of convenience the parties are referred to by their rank before the Tribunal.
4. FACTS:

It is the case of the petitioners that on 12.11.2017, at about 6.30 p.m, deceased-Shivu S/o Bhimaraya along with petitioners Manjunath @ D.Manju and Arjun were proceeding on motor cycle bearing registration No.KA-33/U-3249 (for short 'motor cycle'), towards Gurusunagi Village on Yadgir-Shahapur Main Road.
It was ridden by deceased, whereas the other two petitioners were pillion riders.

When they were near land of Sanna Nagalappa near Gurusunagi Cross, driver of Chevrolet Tavera bearing registration No.MH-46/D-0209 ('offending vehicle' for short) came from Yadgir side, in a high speed, in a rash or negligent manner and dashed against the motor cycle from its back.
Due to the impact, deceased as well as the other two petitioners sustained grievous injuries.
Deceased died on the spot.
4.1 It is further case of the petitioners in MVC.No.117/2018, that deceased was hale and healthy.
He was aged 25 years and working as a coolie earning Rs.10,000/- p.m. and contributing to the family.
Petitioners are the mother and brother of deceased.
They were dependent on him.
4.2 The petitioner in MVC.No.118/2018 has contended that at the time of accident, he was aged 27 years and hale and healthy.
He was earning Rs.10,000/- p.m. doing coolie.
4.3 Petitioner in MVC.No.119/2018 has also contended that at the time of accident, he was aged 19 years, hale and healthy and earning Rs.10,000/- p.m. 4.4
As owner and insurer, respondent Nos.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.

5. Respondents appeared and filed separate written statements disputing the age, occupation,
income of the deceased as well as the other two petitioners and that accident occurred due to the rash or negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle.
They have contended that the accident occurred due to the negligence of deceased.
6. Based on these pleadings, the Tribunal has framed necessary issues.

7. In MVC.No.117/2018, petitioner No.1 is examined as PW-1 and Ex.P1 to 5 are marked.
8.

In MVC.No.118/2018 the petitioner is examined as PW-2 and relied upon to Ex.P6 to 17.
9.
In MVC.No.119/2018, petitioner is examined as PW-3 and he has relied upon Ex.P18 to 23.

However, in MVC.No.117/2018 the Tribunal held that the deceased has also contributed towards the accident and quantified his negligence at 20%, whereas the driver of the offending vehicle was responsible for remaining 80% of the negligence and as such reduced the compensation by 20%.

16. However, so far as the petitioners in MVC.No.118/2018 and MVC.No.119/2018 are concerned,
the Tribunal has held that as the third parties, in the absence of owner and insurer of the motor cycle being parties to the petition, based on Khenyei Vs. New India Assurance Co. Ltd and Ors.1 (Khenyei's case), the Tribunal held that they are at liberty to recover the entire compensation from respondent No.2.
17.

entities.text: Khenyei Vs. New India Assurance Co. Ltd

sentences.text: Respondents have not challenged the impugned judgment and awards.

18. The petitioners have come up with these appeals contending that having regard to the fact that the accident is of the year 2017, the notional income considered in all the three petitions are on the lower side.

So far as injured petitioners are concerned, they have also contended that looking to the nature of the injuries suffered which has resulted in permanent partial disability, the compensation granted under the 2015 (2) TAC 677 (SC) remaining heads are also on the lower side and have sought for enhancement.
19. On the other hand, learned counsel for respondent No.2 supported the impugned judgment and awards and have sought for dismissal of the appeals.

20. Heard arguments and perused the record.
21.
Having regard to the grounds urged by the petitioners it is necessary to examine whether the compensation granted is just and reasonable or it calls for interference.

22. MFA No.200106/2021 (MVC No.117/2018):
So far as MFA.No.200106/2021 (MVC.No.117/2018) is concerned, the Tribunal has correctly considered the age of the deceased as 25 years and appropriate multiplier Maheshwari @ Maheshamma And Anr vs Abdul Khadeer And Anr on 20 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/166538679/
6 18.

sentences.text: Since the petitioners have not produced any evidence with regard to the exact income of the deceased, the Tribunal is justified in considering it on notional basis.
However, having regard to the fact that the accident is of the year 2017, the income ought to have been taken at Rs.10,250/-.
Since the deceased was aged below 40 years and was doing coolie, as per Magma General Insurance Company Limited Vs.

entities.text: Magma General Insurance Company Limited Vs.
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Nanu Ram Alias Chuhru Ram And Others2 (Magma's case)
, 40% of his income is required to be added towards loss of future prospects, which the Tribunal has failed to take into consideration.
Therefore, notional income required to be taken is Rs.14,350/-.
Since deceased was a bachelor, 50% of his income is required to be deducted towards his personal and living expenses.
With these components, the compensation under the head loss of dependency is Rs.14,350 x 12 x 18 x 50% = Rs.15,49,800/-.
23. The Tribunal has granted compensation in a sum of Rs.50,000/- under the head loss of love and (2018) 18 SCC 130 affection.

However, as per the decision of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in National Insurance Company Limited vs. Pranay Sethi and others3 (Pranay Sethi's case) and Magma's cases,
petitioner No.1 the mother alone is entitled for compensation in a sum of Rs.40,000/- under the head loss of consortium and as such a sum of Rs.40,000/- is granted under this head and Rs.50,000/- granted under the head loss of love and affection is disallowed.

sentences.text: 24. When substantial compensation is granted under the head loss of dependency, as per Pranay Sethi's and Magma's cases, a sum of Rs.15,000/- each is required to be granted under the head loss to estate and funeral expenses (which includes transportation charges).
Therefore, compensation granted under the head loss to estate is enhanced to Rs.15,000/- and compensation granted under the head funeral expenses is reduced to Rs.15,000/-.
Thus, in all petitioners in MVC.No.117/2018 are entitled for total compensation in a sum of Rs.16,19,800/- as against Rs.6,73,000/- with interest at 6% p.a. as detailed below:

sentences.text: The Tribunal is justified in holding that deceased was also responsible for causing the accident and quantifying it at 20%.
Therefore, petitioners are entitled for remaining 80% of the compensation amount, which works out to Rs.12,95,840/-.

Therefore, respondent No.2 is directed to pay the said amount to petitioners with interest at 6% p.a.
27.
Now coming to the compensation granted in MVC.No.118/2018.
In this case based on records, the Tribunal has correctly taken the age of the petitioner as 27 years and appropriate multiplier 17.

As the accident is of the year 2017, the notional income ought to have been taken at Rs.10,250/- instead of Rs.7,000/- and therefore, the loss of future income is required to be calculated taking the notional income at Rs.10,250/.
After appreciating the evidence of PW-4, the Tribunal has correctly taken the whole body disability at 20%.

With these components, the future loss of income is Rs.10,250 x 12 x 17 x 20% =
Rs.4,18,200/- as against Rs.2,85,600/- granted by the Tribunal.
28.

Based on medical bills, the Tribunal has rightly granted compensation in a sum of Rs.97,612/-
under the head medical expenses and it requires no interference.

Similarly, looking to the nature of injury and period of treatment, compensation granted in a sum of Rs.10,000/- under the head food and nourishment and Rs.11,250/- under the head attendant charges is correct and it also requires no interference.

29. Having regard to the nature of the injury sustained which has resulted in permanent partial disability and when the income is taken at Rs.10,250/-, the compensation granted under the head laid up period in a sum of Rs.11,250/- is on the lower side and the same is enhanced to Rs.30,750/-.

Similarly the compensation for pain and suffering is enhanced to Rs.40,000/- and loss of amenities is enhanced to Rs.30,000/-.
30.
Thus, in all petitioner is entitled for total compensation in a sum of Rs.6,37,812/- as against Rs.4,66,000/- granted by the Tribunal.

31. MFA No.200004/2021 (MVC No.119/2018):
So far as petitioner in MVC.No.119/2018 is concerned, based on the records, the Tribunal has rightly considered the age of petitioner as 25 years and appropriate multiplier 18.
Since the accident is of the year 2017, the income taken at Rs.7,000/- is on the lower side.
It ought to have been taken at Rs.10,250/-.
Appreciating the evidence of PW-4, the Tribunal has correctly assessed the whole body disability at 15%.

With these components, the loss of future income is Rs.10,250 x 12 x 18 x 15% =
Rs.3,32,100/- as against Rs.2,26,800/- granted by the Tribunal.

32. Based on medical bills, the Tribunal has correctly granted compensation in a sum of Rs.8,110/-
under medical expenses and it requires no interference.

Looking to the nature of injury and period of treatment, compensation granted under the head food and nourishment, conveyance and attendant charges in a total sum of Rs.25,250/- is correct and it requires no interference.

However,
at the rate of Rs.10,250/- for a period of three months, petitioner is entitled for compensation in a sum of Rs.30,750/- under the head loss of income during laid up period as against Rs.5,250/-
granted by the Tribunal.
Similarly, the compensation granted under the head pain and suffering and loss of amenities is enhanced to Rs.30,000/- and Rs.20,000/- respectively.
33. Thus, in all petitioner is entitled for total compensation in a sum of Rs.4,46,210/- as against Rs.2,95,000/- granted by the Tribunal with interest at 6% p.a. as detailed below:

sentences.text: Though in the present case so far as the deceased is concerned, he has contributed towards the cause of the accident and as such his legal representatives are not entitled to recover compensation to the extent of his contribution.

However,
as per Khenyei's case referred to supra so far as petitioners in MVC No.118/2018 and MVC No.119/2018 are concerned, it is a case of composite negligence.
They cannot be held liable for the negligence on the part of the deceased.

Therefore, even in the absence of not arraigning the owner and insurer of the joint tort-feasor, petitioners in MVC.No.118/2018 and MVC.No.119/2018 are entitled to recover entire compensation from respondent No.2 and respondent No.2 is at liberty to recover the remaining 20% of the compensation from the owner or/and insurer of the motor cycle which the deceased was riding at the time of accident, in which he has contributed 20% of the negligence.

35. In the result, the appeals filed requires to be allowed in part and accordingly, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER (i) Appeals are allowed in part.
(ii) Appellants/petitioners in MFA No.200106/ 2021 (MVC No.117/2018) are entitled for total compensation in a sum of Rs.12,95,840/- (being 80% of the total compensation) as against Rs.6,73,000/-
granted by the Tribunal with interest at 6% p.a.
(iii) Appellant/petitioner in MFA No.200005/2021 (MVC No.118/2018) is entitled for total compensation in a sum of Rs.6,37,812/- as against Rs.4,66,000/- granted by the Tribunal with interest at 6%.

(iv) Appellant/petitioner in MFA No.200004/2021 (MVC No.119/2018) is entitled for total compensation in a sum of Rs.4,46,210/- as against Rs.2,95,000/- granted by the Tribunal with interest at 6% p.a.

(v) Respondent No.2-Insurance Company shall deposit the compensation amount within a period of six weeks from the date of this order together with interest at 6% p.a. (minus the amount if already Maheshwari @ Maheshamma And Anr vs Abdul Khadeer And Anr on 20 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/166538679/
10 deposited/paid).
(vi) However respondent No.2 is at liberty to recover 20% of the compensation paid to petitioners in MVC No.118/2018 and MVC No.119/2018 from the owner or/and insurer of the motor cycle, by initiating necessary proceedings against them, if so advised.
(vii) The Registry is directed to send a copy of this judgment to the Tribunal.
